q: Which term matches the definition “Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth”, category “Water pollution”, and fact “Can lead to oxygen depletion”?
e: Eutrophication: Nutrient enrichment causing excessive plant or algal growth. Can lead to oxygen depletion

q: Which term matches the definition “Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels”, category “Pollution”, and fact “Classic example involves mercury”?
e: Biomagnification: Increasing concentration of persistent substances at higher trophic levels. Classic example involves mercury

q: Which term matches the definition “Build-up of a substance within an organism over time”, category “Pollution”, and fact “Occurs when uptake exceeds elimination”?
e: Bioaccumulation: Build-up of a substance within an organism over time. Occurs when uptake exceeds elimination

q: Which term matches the definition “Directional change in community composition over time”, category “Community ecology”, and fact “Can be primary or secondary”?
e: Ecological succession: Directional change in community composition over time. Can be primary or secondary

q: Which term matches the definition “Succession beginning without developed soil”, category “Community ecology”, and fact “May follow lava flows or glacial retreat”?
e: Primary succession: Succession beginning without developed soil. May follow lava flows or glacial retreat

q: Which term matches the definition “Succession where soil remains after disturbance”, category “Community ecology”, and fact “May follow fire or abandoned farming”?
e: Secondary succession: Succession where soil remains after disturbance. May follow fire or abandoned farming

q: Which term matches the definition “Maximum population an environment can sustain over time”, category “Population ecology”, and fact “Depends on resources and environmental conditions”?
e: Carrying capacity: Maximum population an environment can sustain over time. Depends on resources and environmental conditions

q: Which term matches the definition “Resource or condition restricting population growth”, category “Population ecology”, and fact “May be food, water, space or temperature”?
e: Limiting factor: Resource or condition restricting population growth. May be food, water, space or temperature

q: Which term matches the definition “Population growth at a constant proportional rate”, category “Population ecology”, and fact “Produces a J-shaped curve under ideal conditions”?
e: Exponential growth: Population growth at a constant proportional rate. Produces a J-shaped curve under ideal conditions

q: Which term matches the definition “Population growth slowing near carrying capacity”, category “Population ecology”, and fact “Produces an S-shaped curve”?
e: Logistic growth: Population growth slowing near carrying capacity. Produces an S-shaped curve

q: Which term matches the definition “Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another”, category “Species interactions”, and fact “Influences population dynamics”?
e: Predation: Interaction in which one organism kills and consumes another. Influences population dynamics

q: Which term matches the definition “Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource”, category “Species interactions”, and fact “Can occur within or between species”?
e: Competition: Interaction in which organisms seek the same limited resource. Can occur within or between species

q: Which term matches the definition “Interaction benefiting both participating species”, category “Species interactions”, and fact “Pollination is a common example”?
e: Mutualism: Interaction benefiting both participating species. Pollination is a common example

q: Which term matches the definition “Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other”, category “Species interactions”, and fact “One species gains shelter or transport”?
e: Commensalism: Interaction benefiting one species without significant effect on the other. One species gains shelter or transport

q: Which term matches the definition “Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host”, category “Species interactions”, and fact “Usually does not immediately kill the host”?
e: Parasitism: Interaction benefiting a parasite while harming its host. Usually does not immediately kill the host

q: Which term matches the definition “Long-term statistical pattern of weather”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Usually assessed over decades”?
e: Climate: Long-term statistical pattern of weather. Usually assessed over decades

q: Which term matches the definition “Short-term atmospheric conditions”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Includes temperature, precipitation and wind”?
e: Weather: Short-term atmospheric conditions. Includes temperature, precipitation and wind

q: Which term matches the definition “Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases”?
e: Greenhouse effect: Warming caused by atmospheric absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation. Natural process intensified by added greenhouse gases

q: Which term matches the definition “Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Examples include carbon dioxide and methane”?
e: Greenhouse gas: Gas that absorbs and emits infrared radiation. Examples include carbon dioxide and methane

q: Which term matches the definition “Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Fossil-fuel burning raises atmospheric concentration”?
e: Carbon dioxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas from natural and human sources. Fossil-fuel burning raises atmospheric concentration

q: Which term matches the definition “Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Emitted by wetlands, fossil fuels and livestock”?
e: Methane: Potent greenhouse gas with shorter atmospheric lifetime than carbon dioxide. Emitted by wetlands, fossil fuels and livestock

q: Which term matches the definition “Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance”, category “Climate science”, and fact “Major human source is agricultural soil management”?
e: Nitrous oxide: Long-lived greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance. Major human source is agricultural soil management

q: Which term matches the definition “Long-term rise in global average surface temperature”, category “Climate change”, and fact “A major component of current climate change”?
e: Global warming: Long-term rise in global average surface temperature. A major component of current climate change

q: Which term matches the definition “Long-term change in climate state or variability”, category “Climate change”, and fact “Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming”?
e: Climate change: Long-term change in climate state or variability. Human influence is the dominant cause of recent warming

q: Which term matches the definition “Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks”, category “Climate policy”, and fact “Renewable energy and efficiency are examples”?
e: Mitigation: Human intervention to reduce emissions or enhance sinks. Renewable energy and efficiency are examples

q: Which term matches the definition “Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects”, category “Climate policy”, and fact “Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities”?
e: Adaptation: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects. Can reduce harm or exploit beneficial opportunities

q: Which term matches the definition “Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions”, category “Climate and ecology”, and fact “Applies to communities and ecosystems”?
e: Resilience: Capacity to absorb disturbance and retain essential functions. Applies to communities and ecosystems

q: Which term matches the definition “Propensity to be adversely affected”, category “Risk concepts”, and fact “Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity”?
e: Vulnerability: Propensity to be adversely affected. Depends on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity

q: Which term matches the definition “Potential occurrence of an event causing harm”, category “Risk concepts”, and fact “Examples include floods and heatwaves”?
e: Hazard: Potential occurrence of an event causing harm. Examples include floods and heatwaves

q: Which term matches the definition “Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected”, category “Risk concepts”, and fact “A component of climate risk”?
e: Exposure: Presence of people, ecosystems or assets in places that could be affected. A component of climate risk

q: Which term matches the definition “Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration”, category “Atmospheric science”, and fact “Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation”?
e: Ozone layer: Stratospheric region with elevated ozone concentration. Absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation

q: Which term matches the definition “Reduction in stratospheric ozone”, category “Atmospheric science”, and fact “Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons”?
e: Ozone depletion: Reduction in stratospheric ozone. Strongly linked to chlorofluorocarbons

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 1987”?
e: Montreal Protocol: Treaty controlling ozone-depleting substances. Adopted in 1987

q: Which term matches the definition “Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 2015”?
e: Paris Agreement: Climate treaty aiming to strengthen global response to climate change. Adopted in 2015

q: Which term matches the definition “Framework treaty for international climate cooperation”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Opened for signature in 1992”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change: Framework treaty for international climate cooperation. Opened for signature in 1992

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 1997”?
e: Kyoto Protocol: Treaty setting emission targets for many developed countries. Adopted in 1997

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Opened for signature in 1992”?
e: Convention on Biological Diversity: Treaty on conservation, sustainable use and benefit-sharing. Opened for signature in 1992

q: Which term matches the definition “Convention regulating international trade in endangered species”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Uses appendices with different protection levels”?
e: CITES: Convention regulating international trade in endangered species. Uses appendices with different protection levels

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 1971”?
e: Ramsar Convention: Treaty for conservation and wise use of wetlands. Adopted in 1971

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 1989”?
e: Basel Convention: Treaty controlling transboundary movements of hazardous wastes. Adopted in 1989

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty controlling persistent organic pollutants”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 2001”?
e: Stockholm Convention: Treaty controlling persistent organic pollutants. Adopted in 2001

q: Which term matches the definition “Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury”, category “Environmental agreements”, and fact “Adopted in 2013”?
e: Minamata Convention: Treaty protecting health and environment from mercury. Adopted in 2013

q: Which term matches the definition “Land degradation in drylands”, category “Land degradation”, and fact “Driven by climatic variation and human activities”?
e: Desertification: Land degradation in drylands. Driven by climatic variation and human activities

q: Which term matches the definition “Conversion or removal of forest cover”, category “Land degradation”, and fact “Reduces habitat and carbon storage”?
o: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
e: Deforestation: Conversion or removal of forest cover. Reduces habitat and carbon storage

q: Which term matches the definition “Establishment of forest on land not recently forested”, category “Forest management”, and fact “Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned”?
e: Afforestation: Establishment of forest on land not recently forested. Can increase carbon stocks when appropriately planned

q: Which term matches the definition “Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land”, category “Forest management”, and fact “Supports restoration and carbon sequestration”?
e: Reforestation: Re-establishment of forest on recently forested land. Supports restoration and carbon sequestration

q: Which term matches the definition “Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents”, category “Land degradation”, and fact “Can reduce agricultural productivity”?
e: Soil erosion: Removal of topsoil by water, wind or other agents. Can reduce agricultural productivity

q: Which term matches the definition “Accumulation of salts in soil”, category “Land degradation”, and fact “Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage”?
e: Salinization: Accumulation of salts in soil. Often associated with irrigation and poor drainage

q: Which term matches the definition “Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems”, category “Ecosystems”, and fact “Provides flood regulation and habitat”?
e: Wetland: Land saturated or flooded long enough to support adapted ecosystems. Provides flood regulation and habitat

q: Which term matches the definition “Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem”, category “Ecosystems”, and fact “Protects shorelines and stores carbon”?
e: Mangrove: Salt-tolerant coastal forest ecosystem. Protects shorelines and stores carbon

q: Which term matches the definition “Marine ecosystem built largely by reef-forming corals”, category “Ecosystems”, and fact “Highly diverse and sensitive to warming”?
e: Coral reef: Marine ecosystem built largely by reef-forming corals. Highly diverse and sensitive to warming

q: Which term matches the definition “Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals”, category “Marine impacts”, and fact “Often triggered by heat stress”?
e: Coral bleaching: Loss of symbiotic algae or pigments from stressed corals. Often triggered by heat stress

q: Which term matches the definition “Decline in ocean pH caused mainly by absorbed carbon dioxide”, category “Marine impacts”, and fact “Reduces carbonate availability”?
e: Ocean acidification: Decline in ocean pH caused mainly by absorbed carbon dioxide. Reduces carbonate availability

q: Which term matches the definition “Defined marine area managed for conservation”, category “Conservation tools”, and fact “Protection levels vary”?
e: Marine protected area: Defined marine area managed for conservation. Protection levels vary

q: Which term matches the definition “Geographically defined area managed for long-term conservation”, category “Conservation tools”, and fact “May permit different levels of use”?
e: Protected area: Geographically defined area managed for long-term conservation. May permit different levels of use

q: Which term matches the definition “Global assessment system for species extinction risk”, category “Conservation tools”, and fact “Uses categories from Least Concern to Extinct”?
e: IUCN Red List: Global assessment system for species extinction risk. Uses categories from Least Concern to Extinct

q: Which term matches the definition “No reasonable doubt that the last individual has died”, category “Red List category”, and fact “Highest final loss category”?
e: Extinct: No reasonable doubt that the last individual has died. Highest final loss category

q: Which term matches the definition “Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild”, category “Red List category”, and fact “Most severe of the three IUCN threatened categories”?
e: Critically Endangered: Extremely high risk of extinction in the wild. Most severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Which term matches the definition “Very high risk of extinction in the wild”, category “Red List category”, and fact “Threatened category below Critically Endangered and above Vulnerable”?
e: Endangered: Very high risk of extinction in the wild. Threatened category below Critically Endangered and above Vulnerable

q: Which term matches the definition “High risk of extinction in the wild”, category “Red List category”, and fact “Least severe of the three IUCN threatened categories”?
e: Vulnerable: High risk of extinction in the wild. Least severe of the three IUCN threatened categories

q: Which term matches the definition “Resource replenished naturally on human timescales”, category “Resource management”, and fact “Examples include solar and wind energy”?
e: Renewable resource: Resource replenished naturally on human timescales. Examples include solar and wind energy

q: Which term matches the definition “Finite resource not replenished on human timescales”, category “Resource management”, and fact “Examples include fossil fuels”?
e: Non-renewable resource: Finite resource not replenished on human timescales. Examples include fossil fuels

q: Which term matches the definition “Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations”, category “Sustainability”, and fact “Popularized by the Brundtland Commission”?
e: Sustainable development: Development meeting present needs without compromising future generations. Popularized by the Brundtland Commission

q: Which term matches the definition “System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use”, category “Sustainability”, and fact “Emphasizes reuse, repair and recycling”?
e: Circular economy: System aiming to reduce waste and keep materials in use. Emphasizes reuse, repair and recycling

q: Which term matches the definition “Benefits people obtain from ecosystems”, category “Sustainability”, and fact “Include provisioning, regulating and cultural services”?
e: Ecosystem services: Benefits people obtain from ecosystems. Include provisioning, regulating and cultural services

q: Which term matches the definition “Total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or entity”, category “Sustainability metrics”, and fact “Often expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalent”?
e: Carbon footprint: Total greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or entity. Often expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalent

q: Which term matches the definition “Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes”, category “Sustainability metrics”, and fact “Compared with biocapacity”?
e: Ecological footprint: Measure of biologically productive area needed to support consumption and absorb wastes. Compared with biocapacity

q: Which term matches the definition “Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle”, category “Sustainability metrics”, and fact “Covers raw materials through disposal”?
e: Life-cycle assessment: Assessment of environmental impacts across a product's life cycle. Covers raw materials through disposal

q: Which term matches the definition “Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval”, category “Environmental governance”, and fact “Supports informed decision-making”?
e: Environmental impact assessment: Process evaluating likely environmental effects before approval. Supports informed decision-making

q: Which term matches the definition “Introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment”, category “Pollution”, and fact “Can affect air, water or land”?
e: Pollution: Introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment. Can affect air, water or land

q: Which term matches the definition “Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances”, category “Pollution”, and fact “Includes particulate matter and ozone”?
e: Air pollution: Contamination of the atmosphere by harmful substances. Includes particulate matter and ozone

q: Which term matches the definition “Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets”, category “Air pollution”, and fact “PM2.5 penetrates deeply into lungs”?
e: Particulate matter: Mixture of airborne solid particles and liquid droplets. PM2.5 penetrates deeply into lungs

q: Which term matches the definition “Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides”, category “Air pollution”, and fact “Can acidify soils and waters”?
e: Acid rain: Acidic deposition formed mainly from sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Can acidify soils and waters

q: Which term matches the definition “Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health”, category “Air pollution”, and fact “Photochemical smog involves ground-level ozone”?
e: Smog: Air pollution mixture reducing visibility and harming health. Photochemical smog involves ground-level ozone

q: Which term matches the definition “Contamination degrading water quality”, category “Pollution”, and fact “Sources include sewage, industry and agriculture”?
e: Water pollution: Contamination degrading water quality. Sources include sewage, industry and agriculture
